timeline.title: Scott Colom Elected as Mississippi's First Black US Senator Since Reconstruction
timeline.summary: Scott Colom, a Democrat, has been elected as Mississippi's first Black US senator since Reconstruction, defeating incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith in a closely contested race. Colom's victory, confirmed after a narrow margin of fewer than 5,000 votes, marks a significant political shift in the traditionally conservative state. This election also makes him the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Mississippi since 1982.

event_overview.title: About Mississippi Senate Race
event_overview.subject: Mississippi Senate Race
event_overview.summary: The Mississippi Senate race was the 2026 statewide election for Mississippi’s Class II seat in the U.S. Senate. Democrat Scott Colom challenged Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith, with independent Ty Pinkins also on the general-election ballot; news coverage of the event centered on the close post-election count and Colom’s eventual reported victory.

facts.label: Election date and jurisdiction
facts.value: Mississippi held its federal and judicial general election statewide on November 3, 2026; the ballot included one contest for United States Senate.

facts.label: Office and term
facts.value: The contest was for Mississippi’s Class II U.S. Senate seat. U.S. senators serve six-year terms, and Mississippi’s 2026 calendar described the office as a staggered six-year term.

facts.label: Candidates
facts.value: The Mississippi Secretary of State listed Scott Colom as the Democratic candidate, Cindy Hyde-Smith as the Republican candidate, and Ty Pinkins as an independent candidate for the November 3 general election.

facts.label: Incumbency
facts.value: Hyde-Smith held the Class II Mississippi seat before the election; the Senate’s Class II roster identified her as a Republican senator from Mississippi whose term expired in January 2027.

facts.label: Reported outcome
facts.value: On November 11, 2026, the Associated Press reported that it had called the race for Colom after the extended vote-counting process. The Mississippi Secretary of State’s election-results index had not yet posted November 2026 general-election results when consulted.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected timeline covers the late vote-counting period and the reported outcome in this Senate contest, not the full campaign, formal certification or any litigation, or Mississippi’s other 2026 races.
